text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert: p99 tail latency spike on /generate-stream endpoints in us-west-2. error budget burn crossing SLO. auto-run: kv_cache_pressure_check -> high fragmentation detected

maria: seeing p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.4s over the last 3 minutes, streaming stalls visible in traces. multiple customer calls reporting slow chat responses :eyes:

ashok: confirmed. Large spike correlates with increased prefill activity on model-rw-3. KV slab utilization at 92% and slab fragmentation high. evictions up 6x.

lia: is this the same prefill vs decode imbalance we've seen before?

maria: probably. decode tasks are lagging while prefill is flooding cache with small prefixes. prefill hitting many shards, causing cross-shard eviction pressure.

kevin: starting mitigation attempts now: 1) throttle prefill lambda, 2) increase kv slab reclaim threshold on hot nodes, 3) route 20% of traffic to fallback quantized model. will update.

maria: +1 on routing. please move non-critical traffic first (webhook tests, internal dev). keep customer-facing routes minimal impact.

ashok: running this command to lower prefill concurrency on the prefill service: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/prefill-service PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=8
```

lia: applying a soft eviction bump on shard group a2: `--kv-evict-threshold=0.68` (was 0.55). this should free up some frames without full GC.

sre-bot: NOTE: manual eviction threshold change scheduled for 30s, watch for connection churn.

maria: watching dashboards. p95 dropped to 210ms within 90s, p99 down to 1.1s, streaming errors tapering. good signal. keep mitigations in place for 15m and monitor for rebound.

kevin: routed 25% of gen traffic on route /generate-stream -> model-quant-v2. No customer impact observed on that slice.

incident-bot: customer-impact: high for a subset of streaming customers in us-west-2 between 6123456740-6123456860. volume degraded but not full failures.

lia: noted. contacting account owners for top 5 affected customers to prep communications.

maria: handoff plan: oncall->lia in 20m if stable. otherwise stay with ops. also create paging incident for eng-runtime if we can't sustain p99 < 1.5s in 10m.

ashok: quick query I used to correlate prefill vs decode: 
```kql
index=traces service:prefill OR service:decode | stats count() by service, span, pod | sort -count
```
shows prefill spikes aligning with evictions.

kevin: I pushed a temporary runtime tweak to prefer local cache hits before decode fallback on hot nodes: `runtime-opt: prefer_local_kv=true`

maria: rolling that to the three busiest shards. watch for correctness regressions, but risk is low since this only changes eviction order.

sre-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary rollout to 3 pods succeeded, no errors.

lia: telemetry check: no new customer errors in last 2 mins, p99 steady 950ms. I'll stay on and monitor. maria handing off now. :white_check_mark:

maria: handing off to lia — full context above. next steps for eng-runtime/infra: 1) investigate slab fragmentation root cause (allocation patterns), 2) consider targeted slab defrag or per-model reservation, 3) longer-term: better prefill rate limiting by model and shard affinity.

lia: created follow-up ticket ENG-RUNTIME-1327 with summary and logs, assigning to ashok + kevin. will attach the kibana queries and trace ids.

ashok: capture for postmortem: top affected shards: shard-a2, shard-b1; prefill heavy clients: streaming-prefill-worker-12, model-rw-3; suggestion: add backpressure to prefill when slab_util > 0.85.

kevin: I'll open a PR for an autoscale rule to reduce prefill concurrency when kv_evictions_per_min > 1000.

maria: thanks team. if p99 creeps back up we escalate to level-2 and start customer templated outreach. for now continue monitoring, lia will own until 6123456920. :hammer:
